gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, even on DSM 7.3 and later, the Synology DS925+ can create an M.2 NVMe storage pool or cache only with SSDs on Synology's compatibility list (HCL). Fstoppers, which ChatGPT cited, says the opposite for pools.
standout_why: I compared the two cited rivals. Fstoppers (2026-10-28) says DSM 7.3 restored third-party HDD and SATA SSD support, but also says 'You can use third-party NVMe as a storage pool. You cannot use it as cache.' Synology's own DSM 7.3 press release and DS925+ spec page say M.2 pools also need HCL or Synology-verified SSDs, so Fstoppers is wrong on pools. Camera Lookout (2026-09-23) only says to 'confirm every HDD and NVMe model on Synology's current compatibility list' and never states the rule. Neither rival names the QTS 5.2.9 requirement for QNAP's QXG-10G1T 10GbE card, which is the TS-464's upgrade route to 10GbE. Neither mentions the Lightroom Classic 15.4/15.4.1 bug that broke catalog backups to SMB NAS shares. Our current page doesn't state the M.2 rule either: its DS925+ cell just says 'Synology SSDs for pools' with no source.
decides: It confirms the split ChatGPT gave without explaining it. For an HDD archive of 10 TB of RAW files, the DS925+ takes ordinary third-party CMR drives on DSM 7.3+. A photographer who wants a fast M.2 volume on the NAS for current shoots would have to buy SSDs from Synology's list, and the DS925+ still tops out at 2.5GbE with no PCIe slot. That makes the built-in 10GbE UGREEN DXP4800 Plus ($619.99 at UGREEN's store on 2026-11-08) the better pick for editing straight from the NAS, and the DS925+ the pick for a managed archive. If the TS-464 gets a QXG-10G1T card, the NAS needs QTS 5.2.9 or later, and the card sits in a PCIe Gen 3 x2 slot.

findings.label: M.2 NVMe storage pool and cache drive rule (DSM 7.3+)
findings.value: M.2 storage pools and M.2 cache both still require drives on Synology's HCL. Third-party HDDs and SATA drives can be installed and used to create storage pools.
findings.source_title: Synology Releases DiskStation Manager 7.3 ... Expanded Storage Flexibility (Synology press release, 2025-10-08, updated Oct 13)
findings.note: Footnote 1 quoted: '2025 model-year DiskStation Plus, Value, and J Series running DSM 7.3 will support installation and storage pool creation' with third-party drives; 'Creation of M.2 based storage pool and cache still requires drives on the HCL.' This contradicts the line in the cited Fstoppers guide: 'You can use third-party NVMe as a storage pool.'

findings.label: Spec-page footnotes: M.2 pools, memory, expansion
findings.value: M.2 storage pools need Synology-verified SSDs. Synology won't give full warranty or support with non-Synology RAM. Multiple RAM modules must be identical. The DX525 expansion unit raises it to 9 drives. LAN is 2× 2.5GbE, and the spec page lists no PCIe slot.
findings.note: Quoted: 'Creating M.2 storage pools requires the use of Synology-verified SSDs'; 'Synology will not provide complete product warranty or technical support if non-Synology memory modules are used'; 'DS925+/DS925neo+ supports up to 9 drives with a Synology DX525 Expansion Unit, sold separately.' The same page also lists a DS925neo+ variant with non-ECC RAM.

findings.label: Latest DSM firmware for this model
findings.value: DSM 7.4.1-90080 Update 1, released 2026-10-12. The 7.3 branch's latest is 7.3.2-86009 Update 5, released the same day. The DS925+ isn't on any release's list of excluded models.
findings.source_title: Synology DSM release notes for DS925+ (release-note API)
findings.note: DSM 7.3-81180 is dated 2025-10-08. None of the 7.3/7.4 release-note entries mention drive policy. That rule is only in the press release footnote.

findings.label: PCIe slot, M.2, RAM and 10GbE path
findings.value: One PCIe Gen 3 x2 slot. 2× M.2 2280 PCIe Gen 3 x1. 2× DDR4 SODIMM, 16 GB max (2× 8 GB). 2× 2.5GbE; 10GbE and 5GbE only through a PCIe card. 3-year warranty, but bundled accessories and expansion cards get 1 year.
findings.note: Quoted: 'Use only QNAP memory modules to maintain system performance and stability.' The page lists QM2-2P and QXG-10G/25G cards as optional accessories but has no lane-sharing footnote.

findings.label: Firmware needed for QNAP's QXG-10G1T 10GbE card
findings.value: QTS 5.2.9 or later, or QuTS hero h5.2.9 or later. One RJ45 port running at 10/5/2.5/1 GbE and 100 Mb.
findings.note: The page's OS line: 'NAS: QTS 5.2.9 (or later), QuTS hero h5.2.9 (or later).' For use in a PC it lists Windows 11 25H2 and Ubuntu 20.04/22.04 with the r8127 driver. It doesn't list macOS, so on a Mac it isn't a NAS-to-Mac direct option. It points to QNAP's compatibility list for supported NAS models.

findings.label: Lightroom Classic catalog backups to SMB NAS shares
findings.value: Backups failed in LrC 15.4 and 15.4.1 at the compression step, in reports from macOS 26. Adobe says the August 2026 (x.5) release fixed it.
findings.source_title: P: LrC 15.4 & 15.4.1 Cannot create catalog backups directly on SMB NAS shares (Adobe Community)
findings.note: Adobe employee Rikk Flohr posted a pinned reply on 2026-08-04: 'The August release (x.5) contains an update regarding this issue.' Users confirmed the fix on 2026-08-04 and 2026-09-06. The workaround on 15.4.x is to back up to a local drive and copy the file to the NAS. The thread doesn't say whether a separate report of linear DNG corruption from 'Update DNG Preview & Metadata' on SMB shares is fixed too.
